properties.decision:
DECIDED 2026-08-12 by Anthony. OPTION A, knowingly and as a first step. Originally recorded as brainstorming under the question "should closing a session be a SKILL the user types, when the accepted requirement says the user must never be the trigger?" — that question is now answered.

⭐⭐ HIS DECIDING ARGUMENT, AND IT INVERTS THE TENSION THIS NODE WAS BUILT AROUND. His words: "I don't mind the capture-session skill being manual and I can use it as I see fit throughout a session. I would prefer it be automatically done by the agent, but as seen elsewhere, then it is dependent upon the agent remembering or placing hooks to do so... so just being able to run this manually myself as a first step is fine with me."

The node above recorded option A as CONCEDING the central clause of `req:skill-use-survives-a-long-session` ("the user must never be the trigger"). Anthony's reasoning reframes that: options B and C depend on THE AGENT REMEMBERING — and agent forgetting is the documented, four-times-observed failure this whole thread exists because of (`epoch:skill-use-still-needs-reminding`, `chg:user-is-still-the-reminder`, `fact:second-user-report-2026-08-11`, and his own habit). ⇒ THE MANUAL TRIGGER IS NOT THE WEAK OPTION. It is the only one whose reliability does not rest on the thing that keeps failing. A human who types a skill remembers; the mechanism proposed to replace him is the one with the measured defect rate.

📌 THE CLAUSE IS STILL CONCEDED, AND THAT IS RECORDED HONESTLY. `req:skill-use-survives-a-long-session` remains ACCEPTED and still says the user must never be the trigger. This decision does not amend it, does not weaken it, and does not close it. It ships a manual trigger AS A FIRST STEP while the requirement stands unmet — which is the accurate state, and better stated than papered over.

═══ WHAT THIS DECIDES ═══

A `capture-session` skill the user types, served like every other skill, invocable AT ANY POINT IN A SESSION and not only at the end — his words, "I can use it as I see fit throughout a session". That clause was NOT in the original option A and it matters: it directly answers counter-argument ⚠️2 ("session end is the worst moment to ask, and this session is the evidence"), because a skill usable mid-session is capture-as-you-go with a defined contract rather than a closing sweep over a compacted transcript.

═══ WHAT THIS DOES NOT DECIDE ═══
  • OPTION C REMAINS THE DESTINATION. "First step" is his phrasing. The skill defining WHAT capture means is precisely the half C needs; a later hook deciding WHEN sits on top of it without rework. Choosing A does not foreclose C — it builds C's first half.
  • ⚠️1 WHO JUDGES "ANYTHING IMPORTANT" is untouched and is the skill's hardest content problem. The skill must STATE ITS CRITERIA rather than ask an agent to introspect on the significance of its own session.
  • ⚠️3 THE CONNECTIVE TISSUE HAS NO NATURAL NODE — still true, still unresolved, and now load-bearing in a way it was not before: a skill that captures must write SOMETHING somewhere. `cap:session-memory` stays PLANNED.

═══ THE ROADS NOT TAKEN (kept, per brainstorm doctrine) ═══
B — automatic at the Stop hook. Not rejected; deferred. Its mechanism exists and works (it blocked this very session), but it fires per-TURN and cannot tell design-relevant work from any other edit.
C — both, split by role. THE DESTINATION, not a rejection.
D — build `cap:session-memory` instead. Not taken as a substitute, but the skill must answer D's question — what gets written — before it is worth much.
properties.name: SETTLED — a capture-session skill the user types, chosen as the FIRST STEP because it is the only trigger that does not depend on the mechanism that keeps failing
properties.rationale: Captured because the trigger question is genuinely open while the content question is not: dec:idea-is-session-context-already-in-the-graph settled that the connective tissue is what only the session holds, and cap:session-memory has been planned since 2026-07-25 with no trigger. What makes this worth its own node is the tension rather than the idea — req:skill-use-survives-a-long-session is accepted and says the user must never be the trigger, and a skill the user types institutionalises exactly that. Recorded with the counter-arguments beside it, including that this session was compacted, which makes session-end the worst moment to ask for a faithful account of session start.
